chunks: What the Shaykh — may God the Exalted support him — informed me: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman, from Sama'a, who said:
I asked him about running water into which urine is passed. He said: "There is no harm."
And it [the hadith] indicates that avoiding it is preferable.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: preferable, more meritorious (superlative of fadl, indicating a recommended but not obligatory action)
key_terms.اَلاِجْتِنَابَ: avoidance, abstention (refraining from use even where technically permitted)
key_terms.اَلْجَارِي: flowing/running (the juridically significant category of moving water, deemed self-purifying by many jurists)

ai.seo_question: Is running water into which urine has been passed considered ritually pure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Sama'a ibn Mihran queries the Imam about the ritual status of running water into which urine has been passed. The Imam issues a permissive ruling with the standard formula 'no harm,' while Shaykh al-Tusi appends his own commentary that abstaining from such water is nonetheless the superior course.
